ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Isaac Newton Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for a year of poor sleep and appetite, two weeks of near-sleeplessness, and suspicious thoughts about friends, in a researcher who heats mercury and other metals. Concerns: He has barely slept for two weeks, eats little, and feels he has lost his former steadiness of mind; He wrote angry letters to friends he now thinks he wronged, and wants to make amends; He asks whether the metals in his laboratory have poisoned him. [S]

tr.td: A year of poor sleep and poor appetite with 4 kg weight loss, two weeks of near-total sleeplessness, low spirits, and suspicious thoughts that colleagues and friends were plotting against him, now partly doubted; under evaluation for depression, a toxic cause, and other medical causes

S — Synthetic presenting concern echoing the poor sleep, poor appetite, distress, and retracted suspicions documented in his letters of September 1693; superseded by the diagnoses at the second visit.
Occupational exposure to elemental and inorganic mercury, with lesser exposure to lead, antimony, and arsenic compounds, from heating metals in an unventilated private laboratory
S — Synthetic modern exposure echoing his documented chemical and alchemical work with metals, including mercury; no level of historical exposure is asserted.

Major depressive disorder, single episode, severe, without psychotic features (PHQ-9 20 at intake): a year of poor sleep and appetite with weight loss, low mood, poor concentration, and suspicious ideas held with partial insight; medical causes excluded; the contribution of low-level mercury exposure is uncertain

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis. His sleeplessness, poor appetite, distress, and melancholy in 1693 are documented (D); calling them major depression is a modern reading, and mercury poisoning and other explanations proposed later are disputed (R).
Chronic insomnia comorbid with depression: sleep onset and maintenance difficulty for a year, with two weeks of near-total sleeplessness before intake
S — Synthetic diagnosis echoing his documented sleeplessness.

Raised urine mercury from occupational exposure (24-hour urine 46 ug/L, 41 ug/g creatinine; blood 9.4 ug/L) without tremor, gingivitis, erethism, neuropathy, or kidney injury; below the levels linked to overt toxicity
S — Synthetic result echoing his documented work with mercury; it does not assert that he was poisoned (see CLM-0011, R, disputed).
Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) with a low-grade fever, sore throat, and cough, a week after starting sertraline; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent illness at an unscheduled visit; it echoes, without asserting, his documented mention of a distemper that was epidemical that summer (CLM-0008).

list.item: Occupation: professor of mathematics at a university college for about 25 years; for many years has also run a private chemistry laboratory in an outbuilding beside his college rooms, where he heats and distils metals and their ores in a furnace, often through the night [S]

Exposure history: heats elemental mercury in open crucibles and makes amalgams with gold and other metals; roasts antimony ore and works with lead and, occasionally, arsenic sulfide in closed vessels; no fume hood, local exhaust, or respirator; spilled mercury is swept up with a brush; he eats and drinks at the bench; sessions of six to ten hours several nights a week; the last session was three days before this visit [S]
Never married; lives alone in college rooms next to the laboratory; a small circle of friends and correspondents, from several of whom he has recently withdrawn [S]
Never smoker; one glass of wine a week or less (AUDIT-C 1); no cannabis or other drugs; about four cups of tea a day; no supplements or folk remedies [S]
No firearms; the laboratory holds mercury, arsenic, and other toxic chemicals [S]

Ten-day review of metal and laboratory results, diagnosis, start of treatment, and occupational and environmental medicine consultation

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Workup for medical and toxic causes: blood count, metabolic panel, TSH, vitamin B12, MoCA, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio and dipstick protein, blood mercury, 24-hour urine mercury with creatinine, and blood lead; examination for tremor, gingivitis, stomatitis, and neuropathy; no provoked (chelator-challenge) urine test and no broad metal screen
GL-CMID-2026, GL-APA-DEP-2019, GL-MDD-2022, GL-ATSDR-HG-2018, GL-NIOSH-HG, GL-ACMT-2010, GL-ACMT-CHEL-2013

Removal from exposure now: stop all heating of metals, close the laboratory, and do not sleep in the adjoining rooms until they are checked; the university environmental health and safety office to measure mercury vapor, decontaminate, and remove the mercury and arsenic compounds

Suicide and violence risk assessment with a safety plan: warning signs, coping steps, people to contact, the clinic number, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline; toxic chemicals out of reach; safety reviewed at every visit
Occupational and environmental medicine (medical toxicology) consultation on the meaning of the mercury results, chelation, the workplace hazard assessment, and a safe return to laboratory work

Sleep: cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (a fixed rising time, a sleep window, out of bed after 20 minutes awake, no dozing in the evening chair, no night work); no hypnotics or sedating antihistamines

Shared decision on depression treatment: sertraline 50 mg each morning with weekly cognitive behavioral therapy; PHQ-9 at every visit; an increase if the response is under 50 percent after six to eight weeks; continue for at least six to twelve months after remission

Collaborative care: the clinic's psychiatrist reviews his PHQ-9, safety, and medicine each week with the care manager, and sees him in person if psychotic features, suicidal thoughts, or thoughts of harming others appear, or if he does not respond

Exposure follow-up: repeat 24-hour urine mercury and blood mercury four to six weeks after removal and again at three months; creatinine and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio at three months; return to laboratory work only with a fume hood, a mercury spill kit, no food at the bench, and urine mercury below the biological exposure index
Nutrition: three regular meals a day, weight at every visit
Toxic and other medical causes assessed by the second visit
Blood count, metabolic panel, TSH, vitamin B12, kidney tests, blood lead, and MoCA normal; blood and urine mercury raised from his work, below levels linked to overt toxicity
No further exposure to mercury and other metals until the laboratory is made safe
Laboratory closed since intake; urine mercury falling
Response (PHQ-9 down by at least 50 percent) by eight to twelve weeks of treatment, then remission (PHQ-9 below 5)
PHQ-9 14 after three weeks of sertraline, 30 percent below baseline
No suicidal thoughts and no thoughts of harming others
At least six hours of sleep most nights without hypnotics
About five and a half hours by the third chronic-care visit

list.item: Independent in all activities of daily living; still teaching, but has stopped answering letters, eats one small meal a day, and has spent nights at the furnace or lying awake [S]
Thin, slightly unkempt, tired; guarded at first, then courteous and engaged; speech normal in rate and volume; no psychomotor agitation or slowing [S]

Mood "out of sorts and worn down"; affect constricted and anxious; thought process linear; preoccupied with the belief that a friend tried to entangle him in gossip and that others planned to buy him off with a post, which he now partly doubts ("I may have been unjust"); no fixed delusions; no hallucinations; no thoughts of death or self-harm; he once said in anger that a friend would be better dead, regrets it, and has no thoughts or intent of harming anyone; MoCA 27; insight partial and improving; judgment fair [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-09-28: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. No suicidal ideation, intent, plan, or behavior (C-SSRS screen negative; PHQ-9 item 9 scored 0). No thoughts or intent of harming others; an angry remark about a friend is regretted, with no history of violence. Severe insomnia and depressive symptoms raise risk, so: outpatient care with a safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number, the laboratory closed today and its mercury and arsenic compounds to be removed by the university safety office, and review at every visit [S]
